rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yunus describes himself as unjust regarding God's majesty: his own description cannot do justice to the majesty of divine oneness.
rows.anchor: في وصف جلالك إذ وصفي لا يليق بعزة وحدانيتك

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet's confession that he cannot enumerate God's praise explains Yunus's modest confession.
rows.anchor: سيد المرسلين حيث قال : "لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك"

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet said, Do not prefer me over my brother Yunus.
rows.anchor: قال عليه السلام : "لا تفضلوني على أخي يونس"

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After experiencing this state, Yunus feared he would not regain what he had attained in the world, became distressed when the Real was veiled from him, and called for rescue.
rows.anchor: فغاب الحق عنه فاهتم ودعا بالنجاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answered Yunus's prayer, which implicitly confessed his fault in the gentlest and most emphatic manner.
rows.anchor: دعاءه الذي في ضمن الاعتراف بالذنب على ألطف وجه وآكده

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: As God rescued Yunus from bodily darkness, He rescues the believer's supported spirit from veils of soul, body, and world, enabling remembrance of oneness and vicegerency in seen and unseen realms.
rows.anchor: وفيه إشارة إلى أنه تعالى كما أجاب يونس ونجاه من ظلمات عالم الأجسام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith promises that any distressed person who calls with this supplication will be answered.
rows.anchor: "ما من مكروب يدعو بهذا الدعاء إلا استجيب له"

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Yunus was saved only through his own admission of wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: وعن الحسن ما نجاه والله إلا إقراره على نفسه بالظلم

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies this confession of God's oneness as the greatest name: invoking it brings an answer and asking by it brings a gift.
rows.anchor: وفي "صحيح المستدرك" قال عليه السلام : "اسم الله الأعظم الذي إذا دعى به أجاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God relieved Yunus of the distress of being swallowed and of the sea when the fish cast him ashore; reports give his time inside as four hours, three, seven, or forty days, and describe a journey to remote seas and the earth's seventh depth.
rows.anchor: من غم الالتقام والبحر بأن قذفه الحوت إلى الساحل بعد أربع ساعات أو ثلاثة أيام أو سبعة أو أربعين

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say the fish's head remained above the water and its mouth stood open.
rows.anchor: كان رأس الحوت فوق الماء وفمه مفتوحا

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a report traced to the Prophet, God ordered the fish not to injure Yunus; sea creatures' praise led him to glorify God, angels interceded after hearing him, and the fish cast him ashore.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي هريرة رضي الله عنه يرفعه أوحى الله إلى الحوت أن خذه ولا تخدش له لحما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage evokes a soul moving from spiritual qualities toward lordship, returning to its Lord under an eternal promise fulfilled forever.
rows.anchor: ومن وصف الروحانية إلى وصف الربوبية بجذوة ارجعي إلى ربك وعدا علينا في الأزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Zabur is the scripture given to David, as stated in 4:163.
rows.anchor: وهو كتاب داود عليه السلام كما قال :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the Reminder means after the Torah; every heavenly book is called a reminder.
rows.anchor: بعدما كتبنا في التوراة لأن كل كتاب سماوي ذكر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Zabara means writing in bold strokes; any heavily written book is a zabur, though the term is especially used for David's revealed book.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب زبرت الكتاب كتبته كتابة غليظة وكل كتاب غليظ الكتابة

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Another view takes zabur to mean any divine book that is difficult to comprehend.
rows.anchor: بل الزبور كل كتاب يصعب الوقوف عليه من الكتب الإلهية

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A further view distinguishes the Zabur, limited to rational wisdom without legal rulings, from a book containing both rulings and wisdom; David's Zabur lacks rulings.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم اسم للكتاب المقصور على الحكمة العقلية دون الأحكام الشرعية

rows.speaker: القاموس
rows.claim: Al-Qamus defines zabur as a written book, gives zubur as its plural, and identifies it as David's book.
rows.anchor: الزبور الكتاب بمعنى المزبور والجمع زبر وكتاب داود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous servants generally inherit the land after disbelievers are expelled; this promises the establishment of religion and honor for its adherents, as in 24:55.
rows.anchor: عامة المؤمنين بعد إجلاء الكفار

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the inherited earth is Paradise, supported by the verse describing believers inheriting a place in Paradise.
rows.anchor: أن المراد أرض الجنة كما ينبىء عنه قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: عرائس البقلي
rows.claim: In primordial knowledge, Paradise's lands are inherited by the righteous for their rewards and ranks, while witnessing eternal divine majesty is the inheritance of knowers and lovers; the former behold servanthood, the latter lordship.
rows.anchor: قال في "عرائس البقلي" : كان في علم الأزلية أن أرض الجنان ميراث عباده الصالحين

rows.speaker: سهل
rows.claim: Sahl says God claims them as His own and calls them righteous because their inner selves are sincerely His alone, rectified and wholly detached from all besides Him.
rows.anchor: قال سهل أضافهم إلى نفسه وحلاهم بحلية الصلاح معناه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fulfill vows by pledging to turn toward God with sincere seeking and intention.
rows.anchor: فيما عاهدوا الله على التوجه إليه وصدق الطلب والإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inward circumambulation is to circle God with heart and secret, rather than circle anything else; al-Atiq means ancient and is an attribute of God.
rows.anchor: يطوفوا حول الله بقلبهم وسرهم ولا يطوفوا حول ما سواه وأراد بالعتيق القديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That points back to the prescribed matters from God's placing Abraham through the rites of the Ancient House; the verse gathers commanded and prohibited rulings and separates statements or two aspects of one statement.
rows.anchor: الأمر والشأن ذلك الذي ذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sacred inviolabilities are things that may not be violated: God's rulings, duties, practices, and the Sacred Kaaba, mosque, precinct, and month, observed by knowing their obligation and acting accordingly.
rows.anchor: جمع حرمة وهي ما لا يحل هتكه وهو خرق الستر عما وراءه أي أحكامه وفرائضه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reverence benefits its practitioner through reward with God in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: فالتعظيم خير له ثوابا عند ربه أي في الآخرة

rows.speaker: ابن الشيخ
rows.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh reads with his Lord as a sign of reward stored up because the good comes from obeying God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : عند ربه يدل على الثواب المدخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Inwardly, revering God's inviolability means avoiding His prohibitions; obedience brings the servant to Paradise, but reverence brings the servant to God, so it surpasses service as a way of nearness.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن تعظيم حرمات الله هو تعظيم في ترك ما حرمه الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Neglecting service incurs punishment, while violating reverence risks separation; ordinary faults may be forgiven, but breach of inviolability can damage religion and divine oneness.
rows.anchor: ترك الخدمة يوجب العقوبة وترك الحرمة يوجب الفرقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The livestock are the eight pairs of sheep, goats, camels, and cattle, male and female; horses, mules, and donkeys are excluded.
rows.anchor: وهي الأزواج الثمانية على الإطلاق من الضأن اثنين أي الذكر والأنثى ومن المعز اثنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The exception refers to livestock prohibited elsewhere, such as carrion and animals dedicated to other than God; it is connected because it excludes livestock prohibited for a contingent reason, as in 5:3.
rows.anchor: حرمت عليكم الميتة والدم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parenthetical clarification confirms the permission to eat and feed livestock and prevents the mistaken belief that consecration makes them forbidden like game; obey God's limits and do not adopt pagan bans or permit what revelation forbids.
rows.anchor: والجملة اعتراض جيء به تقريرا لما قبله من الأمر بالأكل والإطعام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The filth associated with idols is idol worship itself, to be avoided as one avoids impurities.
rows.anchor: الرجس الذي هو الأوثان يعني عبادتها كما يجتنب الأنجاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rijs means something impure; impurity may be natural, rational, legal, or all three, as with carrion, while wine, gambling, and idols are legally impure.
rows.anchor: والرجس يكون على أربعة أوجه إما من حيث الطبع وإما من جهة العقل

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Awthan are stones that were worshipped.
rows.anchor: والأوثان وهي جمع وثن وهو حجارة كانت تعبد

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some distinguish a sanam, made of wood, gold, or silver in human form, from a wathan, which is not so fashioned.
rows.anchor: الفرق بينه وبين الصنم أن الصنم هو الذي يؤلف من شجر أو ذهب

rows.speaker: الإرشاد
rows.claim: The avoidance command follows from revering God's inviolabilities; livestock permission might prompt consumption, so the text then clarifies what must be avoided and culminates with the gravest prohibitions.
rows.anchor: قال في "الإرشاد" وقوله : {فاجتنبوا} إلخ مرتب على ما يفيده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Avoiding false speech generalizes beyond idol worship, the chief falsehood; polytheists falsely claim idols deserve worship and falsely attribute their animal taboos to God.
rows.anchor: تعميم بعد تخصيص فإن عبادة الأوثان رأس الزور والمشرك يزعم أن الوثن يحق له العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command applies to every kind of false statement and forbids approaching any of it.
rows.anchor: قول الزور كله ولا تقربوا شيئا منه

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet equated false testimony with associating partners with God, repeated the statement three times, and recited this verse.
rows.anchor: عدلت شهادة الزور الإشراك بالله تعالى ثلاثا

rows.speaker: عمر
rows.claim: Umar punished false witnesses with forty lashes, blackened their faces with charcoal, and paraded them through the markets.
rows.anchor: وكان عمر رضي الله عنه يجلد شاهد الزور أربعين جلدة ويسود وجهه بالفحم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zur derives from turning aside, as ifk derives from turning or reversing; falsehood is diverted away from reality.
rows.anchor: والزور من الزور وهو الانحراف كالإفك المأخوذ من الإفك الذي هو القلب

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inwardly, false speech is any spoken claim unsupported by the heart; making a sincere covenant to seek God and then failing it is also false speech.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : قول الزور كل قول باللسان مما لا يساعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Persian verses counsel learning truth from the pure heart, seeking freedom sincerely, keeping faith, bearing blame, and remaining content rather than taking offense.
rows.anchor: طريق صدق بياموز ازآب صافي دل براستي طلب ازادكي جو سرومن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Meccan surah is counted as 110 verses by Basrans and 118 by Kufans.
rows.anchor: مكية وهي مائة وعشر آيات عند البصريين وثماني عشرة عند الكوفيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says that when God created Eden, it spoke the verse's words; God called it a blessed home of the kings of Paradise, the patient poor.
rows.anchor: فقالت : قد أفلح المؤمنون فقال : طوبى لك ، منزل الملوك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The past tense signals certain success, and qad confirms the realization of an outcome believers had already expected from God's grace.
rows.anchor: فصيغة الماضي للدلالة على تحقق الدخول في الفلاح وكلمة قد لإفادة ثبوت ما كان متوقع الثبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Success is lasting in Paradise, attaining one's aim, and escaping harm; aflaha means entering that state, like entering glad tidings, or can mean admitting someone into it.
rows.anchor: والفلاح البقاء والفوز بالمراد والنجاة من المكروه والإفلاح الدخول في ذلك كالإبشار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A passive-voice reading takes aflaha as meaning that believers were admitted into success.
rows.anchor: وقد يجيء متعديا بمعنى الإدخال فيه وعليه قراءة من قرأ على البناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Basic assent to essential teachings such as oneness, prophethood, resurrection, and recompense does not by itself yield true success; it requires faith with all its conditions.
rows.anchor: لما كان الفلاح الحقيقي لا يحصل بمطلق الإيمان وهو التصديق بما علم ضرورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khushu means fear and humility; the worshippers fear God, humble themselves before Him, and keep their eyes fixed on their prayer places.
rows.anchor: أي خائفون من الله متذللون له ملزمون أبصارهم مساجدهم

rows.speaker: المفردات
rows.claim: Al-Mufradat defines khushu as submissiveness, usually visible in bodily limbs, while humility is more often found in the heart.
rows.anchor: في "المفردات" : الخشوع : الضراعة وأكثر ما يستعمل فيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that when the heart is submissive, the limbs become humble.
rows.anchor: فيما ورد : "إذا ضرع القلب خشعت الجوارح"

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: After this verse descended, the Prophet lowered his gaze toward his place of prostration, having previously looked toward the sky during prayer.
rows.anchor: روي : أنه عليه السلام كان إذا صلى رفع بصره إلى السماء

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet saw a worshipper playing with his beard and said that a humble heart would make the limbs humble.
rows.anchor: وأنه رأى مصليا يعبث بلحيته فقال : "لو خشع قلب هذا لخشعت جوارحه"

rows.speaker: النتف
rows.claim: Al-Nutaf regards looking skyward at the opening takbir as disliked because it is a prohibited turn during prayer; outside prayer it is not disliked, since the sky is the direction of supplication and the source of blessings.
rows.anchor: وفي "النتف" : يكره تقليب الوجه إلى نحو السماء عند التكبيرة الأولى

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says the worshipper should look at the prostration place while standing, except in Mecca, where the gaze should fall on the Sacred House.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (رلباب فرموده كه درحالت قيام ديده برسجده كاه بايد نهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith depicts the worshipper standing before the All-Merciful; if he turns away, God asks whom he seeks and calls him back to the better object of attention.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث : "إن العبد إذا قام إلى الصلاة فإنما هو بين يدي الرحمن فإذا التفت

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya maps outward khushu to bowed head, lowered eyes, attentive ear, present measured tongue, folded hands, level bow, restraint from lustful thoughts, and still feet.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : خاشعون أي بالظاهر والباطن

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Inward khushu quiets the soul from passing thoughts, keeps the heart in remembrance and presence, watches over the secret against glancing at created things, and immerses the spirit in love and disclosure of beauty and majesty.
rows.anchor: وأما الباطن : فخشوع النفس سكونها عن الخواطر والهواجس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The trusts and covenants include what people entrust to them or bind themselves to, whether from God or from other people; examples include deposits and duties such as prayer, fasting, and ritual bathing.
rows.anchor: لما يؤتمنون عليه ويعاهدون من جهة الحق أو الخلق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An amana is what a person is entrusted with; an ahd is maintaining and attending to something over time, including a binding compact.
rows.anchor: والأمانة اسم لما يؤتمن عليه الإنسان والعهد حفظ الشيء ومراعاته حالا بعد حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guarding means maintaining and protecting these trusts and covenants in a sound way.
rows.anchor: أي قائمون عليها وحافظون لها على وجه الإصلاح

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Najmiyya identifies the human trust as the divine outpouring received without intermediary, a special honor of humankind; the covenant is the primordial pledge to worship God alone, as in 36:61.
rows.anchor: وفي "التأويلات النجمية" : الأمانة التي حملها الإنسان وهي الفيض الإلهي بلا واسطة

rows.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
rows.claim: Keeping the inner and outer trusts entails worshipping no other than God; desire is the most hateful idol because it makes people worship what they worship besides God.
rows.anchor: راعون بأن لا يخونوا في الأمانات الظاهرة والباطنة ولا يعبدوا غير الله

rows.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says all limbs are trusts: eyes must avoid forbidden sights and reflect, ears avoid idle or obscene speech and attend remembrance, and the tongue avoid backbiting and slander while remembering God.
rows.anchor: قال محمد بن الفضل : جوارحك كلها أمانات عندك أمرت في كل واحدة منها

rows.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl assigns the feet to obedience, the mouth to lawful intake, and the hands to avoiding what is unlawful and not withholding what is good.
rows.anchor: وأمانة الرجل المشي إلى الطاعات والتباعد عن المعاصي

rows.speaker: محمد بن الفضل
rows.claim: Muhammad ibn al-Fadl says the heart's trust is constant regard for God, seeing and witnessing no other and finding repose only in Him.
rows.anchor: وأمانة القلب مراعاة الحق على دوام الأوقات حتى لا يطالع سواه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reflecting on prophets and perfected saints shows that most migrated, since living among unjust people offers no security.
rows.anchor: ولو تفكرت في أحوال الأنبياء وكمل الأولياء لوجدت أكثرهم مهاجرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi thanks God for repeated migrations, for Bursa as his home and a good, forgiving town, and for rescue from unjust opponents; his trial turned into deliverance, subjugation into kindness, and majesty into beauty.
rows.anchor: يقول الفقير : أحمد الله تعالى على نعمه المتوافرة لا سيما على المهاجرة التي وقعت مرارا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The generation established after Noah's people is the people of Ad, as confirmed by the address to them in 7:69.
rows.anchor: أوجدنا وأحدثنا من بعد إهلاك قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarn denotes people of one shared period, those living in the same age.
rows.anchor: والقرن القوم المقترنون من زمن واحد أي أهل زمان واحد

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines the malā as a group united by an opinion, whose presence fills eyes with awe and souls with grandeur.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الملأ الجماعة يجتمعون على رأي فيملؤون العيون روعاء والنفوس دلالة وبهاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The malā are the leading figures of the disbelieving people; their description as disbelievers censures them.
rows.anchor: أي أشراف قومه الكافرين وصفوا بالكفر ذما لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The conjunction wāw rather than fa is used because their speech does not follow directly from the messenger's speech; truth and falsehood coincided, far apart in value.
rows.anchor: وذكره بالواو دون الفاء كما في قصة نوح لأن كلامهم لم يتصل بكلام الرسول

rows.speaker: برهان القرآن
rows.claim: Unlike the Noah passage, this verse places min qawmihi first because its relative clause is longer; delaying the prepositional phrase would confuse the syntax and putting it mid-clause would be awkward.
rows.anchor: قال في "برهان القرآن" : قدم من قومه في هذه الآية وأخر فيما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They denied arrival in the afterlife through resurrection and gathering, or denied meeting its accounting, reward, and punishment.
rows.anchor: بالمصير إلى الآخرة بالبعث والحشر أو بلقاء ما فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God made them comfortable and expanded their worldly ease; the root describes luxuriating in abundance, which can lead to arrogance.
rows.anchor: نعمناهم ووسعنا عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The chiefs spoke to their descendants, misleading them, on account of their abundant wealth and children.
rows.anchor: بكثرة الأموال والأولاد أي قالوا لأعقابهم مضلين لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This refers to Hud, whom the chiefs portray as sharing ordinary human qualities with them.
rows.anchor: أي : هود {إلا بشر مثلكم} في الصفات والأقوال البشرية

words: يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His eating and drinking the same food as them is offered as proof that he is merely human; their Persian gloss argues a prophet should resemble angels and need neither food nor drink.
rows.anchor: أي تشربون منه وهو تقرير للمماثلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call their intellect and judgments lost and deluded because they have degraded themselves.
rows.anchor: عقولكم ومغبونون في آرائكم حيث أذللتم أنفسكم

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi says they regard following a peer as making themselves commanded and led by someone like themselves.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (زيان زد كانيدكه خودرا مأمور ومتبوع مثل خود سازيد)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call obedience to a true messenger who brings happiness in both worlds a loss, while overlooking the greater loss of idol worship.
rows.anchor: انظر كيف جعلوا أتباع الرسول الحق الذي يوصلهم إلى سعادة الدارين خسرانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idhan separates inna from its predicate to emphasize the conditional assertion; the sentence answers an omitted oath.
rows.anchor: وإذن وقع بين اسم إن وخبرها لتأكيد مضمون الشرط والجملة جواب لقسم محذوف

rows.speaker: بعض الفضلاء
rows.claim: Some scholars take idhan as an adverb whose complement was omitted and whose final n compensates for it.
rows.anchor: قال بعض الفضلاء : إذن ظرف حذف منه ما أضيف إليه ونون عوضا

rows.speaker: العيون
rows.claim: Al-Uyun treats idhan as the answer to an omitted condition: if you obey him, then you will be losers.
rows.anchor: وفي "العيون" : إذن جواب شرط محذوف أي إنكم إن أطعتموه إذن لخاسرون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask whether the prophet is promising them resurrection.
rows.anchor: ايا وعده ميدهد شمارا اين يغمبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mīm in mittum is read with kasra from māta-yamātu or with damma from māta-yamūtu.
rows.anchor: بكسر الميم من مات يمات وقرىء بضمها من مات يموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They imagine themselves as dust and bare bones stripped of flesh and sinews; dust comes first because its transformation is more implausible, or because earlier people were dust and later ones bones.
rows.anchor: نخرة مجردة عن اللحوم والأعصاب أي كان بعض أجزائكم من اللحم ونظائره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Bursevi prefers that they mean becoming bones and then dust, since wāw merely joins without fixing the order.
rows.anchor: الظاهر أن مرادهم بيان صيرورتهم عظاما ثم ترابا لأن الواو لمطلق الجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Innakum repeats the earlier assertion for emphasis after a long separation from its predicate, mukhrajun.
rows.anchor: تأكيد للأول لطول الفصل بينه وبين خبره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They would be brought alive out of their graves as they were before.
rows.anchor: أي من القبور أحياء كما كنتم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hayhat is an indeclinable noun meaning far away; repeating it intensifies their claim that resurrection is remote.
rows.anchor: اسم فعل وهو بعد وتكريره لتأكيد البعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say what they are promised will never happen; alternatively, the lām explains the object of their exclamation, as if asked what is so remote.
rows.anchor: لما صوتوا بكلمة الاستبعاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here in is a negating particle meaning mā, so the phrase means this life is only our worldly life.
rows.anchor: إن بمعنى ما ، أي ما الحياة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They describe worldly life as near and perishing.
rows.anchor: أي ما الحياة {الا حياتنا الدنيا} الدانية الفانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase either means some die while others are born until the age ends, or that people experience worldly life and then death with no life afterward.
rows.anchor: أي يموت بعضنا ويولد بعض إلى انقراض العصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny being raised after death, as Hud says they claim; their hearts are blind to the fact that restoration is easier than initial creation and that the creator of existence and nonexistence can restore it.
rows.anchor: بمنشرين بعد الموت كما تزعم يا هود انظر كيف عميت قلوبهم حتى لم يروا أن الإعادة أهون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He refers to Hud, whom they accuse of inventing lies about being sent by God and about resurrection.
rows.anchor: أي : ما هود {إلا رجل افترى على الله كذبا}

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says farī is cutting leather for sewing and repair, while ifrāʾ is spoiling; iftirāʾ can mean either but is more often corruption, hence Quranic use for lies, idolatry, and oppression.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : الفري قطع الجلد للخرز والإصلاح والإفراء للإفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people say they do not believe Hud's claims.
rows.anchor: بمصدقين فيما يقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After despairing of their belief, Hud asks God to aid him against them and avenge him because they denied him and persisted in denial.
rows.anchor: هود بعد ما يئس من إيمانهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Amma qalil means after a short time; mā is an extra particle between the preposition and noun that reinforces the sense of smallness.
rows.anchor: أي عن زمان قليل وما مزيدة بين الجار والمجرور لتأكيد معنى القلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb means they will become, referring to the unbelieving deniers.
rows.anchor: أي ليصيرن أي الكفار المكذبون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They will regret their disbelief and denial when they witness the punishment.
rows.anchor: على الكفر والتكذيب وذلك عند معاينتهم العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gabriel's tremendous cry split their hearts and killed them; sayha means a raised voice.
rows.anchor: صيحة جبريل صاح عليهم صيحة هائلة تصدعت منها قلوبهم فماتوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although this suggests Thamud, since Ad were destroyed by a sterile wind, the author reconciles it by suggesting the intensified wind also brought a terrible cry; he cites a report that Shaddad and his family were destroyed by a heavenly cry approaching Iram, or that the cry itself means torment and death.
rows.anchor: فإن قلت : هذا يدل على أن المراد بالقرن المذكور في صدر القصة ثمود قوم صالح

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn glosses the cry as the cry of punishment.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" : فأخذتهم صيحة العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With truth attaches to the taking and means it occurred by an established, unavoidable decree.
rows.anchor: متعلق بالأخذ أي بالوجه الثابت الذي لا دافع له

rows.speaker: الجلالين
rows.claim: Al-Jalalayn explains the phrase as by God's command.
rows.anchor: وفي "الجلالين" : بالأمر من الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God transformed them into worthless flood debris.
rows.anchor: أي كغثاء السيل لا ينتفع به وهو ما يحمله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ghuthaʾ is what a flood carries along its surface: foam, leaves, and sticks; the idiom 'the valley swept him away' means that someone perished.
rows.anchor: وهو ما يحمله السيل على وجهه من الزبد والورق والعيدان

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Kashifi glosses the image as destroying and annihilating them, like debris a flood casts aside and leaves black and worn.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (غثاء : ون خاشاك آب آورده يعني هلاك كرديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase may report their ruin or curse them.
rows.anchor: {فبعدا للقوم الظالمين} يحتمل الإخبار والدعاء

rows.speaker: الكاشفي
rows.claim: Al-Kashifi glosses it as banishment from God's mercy for the hated oppressors.
rows.anchor: قال الكاشفي : (س دوري باد ازرحمت خداي مركروه ستمكارانرا)

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Buʿd means perishing; it is a verbal noun rarely used with an expressed governing verb, and the lām indicates the one addressed by the curse.
rows.anchor: وبعدا مصدر بعد إذا هلك وهو من المصادر التي لا يكاد يستعمل ناصبها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse signals the fate of worldly people who rebel against God and transgress against messengers.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشارة إلى أن أهل الدنيا حين بغوا في الأرض وطغوا على الرسل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Though messengers share ordinary people's food and drink, they do not eat with worldly excess: God's people eat without extravagance, unlike disbelievers who consume sevenfold.
rows.anchor: وقالوا لرسلهم ما قالوا لا يعلمون أن الرسل وأهل الله وإن كانوا يأكلون مما يأكل أهل الدنيا

rows.speaker: النبي ﷺ
rows.claim: The Prophet says the believer eats in one intestine and the disbeliever in seven.
rows.anchor: قال النبي عليه السلام : "المؤمن يأكل في معى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's people also eat and drink through the mouths of their hearts from divine provision during their nights with their Lord.
rows.anchor: بل أهل الله يأكلون ويشربون بأفواه القلوب مما يطعمهم ربهم ويسقيهم

rows.speaker: أفتاده أفندي
rows.claim: Aftada says the Prophet stayed with his Lord and received nourishment from varied divine disclosures; outward eating served his weak community, while the stone he strapped on was to keep his subtle spirit in the world for guidance, not because of hunger.
rows.anchor: قال حضرة الشيخ الشهير بأفتاده أفندي قدس سره : كان عليه السلام يبيت عند ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers had the worst traits: disbelief in the Creator and resurrection, immersion in worldly love, and oppression; their destruction came because of their injustice.
rows.anchor: وقد وصف الله الكفار بشر الصفات وهي الكفر بالخالق وبيوم القيامة والانغماس في حب الدنيا

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say one who submits from fear of punishment or desire for reward submits unwillingly, while one who knows and loves the reward-giver rather than the reward itself submits freely; this is the form valued by God's people.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : من طالع الثواب والعقاب فاسلم رغبة ورهبة فهو إنما أسلم كرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A thoughtful person should reflect on the Quran, purify faith, and reach knowledge, certainty, and even direct witnessing; God sent His messenger with truth, and anything beyond truth is error.
rows.anchor: فعلى العاقل أن يتدبر القرآن فيخلص الإيمان ويصل إلى العرفان والإيقان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The truth they dislike includes the Quran brought by the Prophet; the hypothetical means that if revelation conformed to disbelievers' desires, the heavens, earth, and their inhabitants would be corrupted and lose order, since order depends on truth such as Islam, oneness, and justice.
rows.anchor: الذي كرهوه ومن جملته ما جاء به عليه السلام من القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The inhabitants included are angels, humans, and jinn, and the cosmos would lose all order if governed by their desires.
rows.anchor: من الملائكة والإنس والجن وخرجت عن الصلاح والانتظام

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some say that without God's command to oppose the ego, people would follow their passions, stray from servitude, abandon divine commands, and be led by desire into Hell.
rows.anchor: قال بعضهم : لولا أن الله أمر بمخالفة النفوس ومباينتها لاتبع الخلق أهواءهم
